subject: StagedStan: Python package for running Stan using compiled executables

messages.author: 51b52a084c2df35c
messages.subject: StagedStan: Python package for running Stan using compiled executables
parts:
Dear all,

I would like to point out this small Python package I wrote:

   https://github.com/JohannesBuchner/stagedstan

Unlike PyStan, it uses the make process of Stan (i.e. produces and runs executables), and actively stores outputs.

From the Readme file:
  • StagedStan works similar to "make", namely in a deterministic fashion.
  • Runs consist of compilation, optimization and sampling (starting from the best fit).
  • When aborted, it continues where it was stopped.
  • Unlike PyStan, all results are stored in a file structure.
  • Each output is uniquely associated to the Stan code, data and seed used. If neither of them change, the result is not re-computed.
  • This also allows you to execute Stan on another machine, and to copy the output over.
  • StagedStan can parse the summary files of Stan runs, and write data dump files.
  • StagedStan allows the input of data from Python (e.g. numpy arrays).
Perhaps it is useful for someone else too. Fork and play around with it.

Kind regards,
         Johannes

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] StagedStan: Python package for running Stan using compiled executables
parts:
Thanks for the references and package. Some comments
below.

On 2/3/14, 2:07 AM, Johannes wrote:
> Dear all,
>
> I would like to point out this small Python package I wrote:
>
> https://github.com/JohannesBuchner/stagedstan
>
> Unlike PyStan, it uses the make process of Stan (i.e. produces and runs executables), and actively stores outputs.
>
> From the Readme file:
>

> * StagedStan works similar to "make", namely in a deterministic fashion.

Is there something non-deterministic about PyStan?

> * Runs consist of /compilation/, /optimization/ and /sampling/ (starting from the best fit).
> * When aborted, it continues where it was stopped.

This is tricky because we don't yet have a way in Stan to read in
the adaptation state and CmdStan only saves it in a comment in
the output CSV. We're working on reading in the adaptation state so
it's possible to just generate more draws without having to rerun
adaptation. (Having said that, the reason we didn't worry too much
about it the first time around is that if the initial effective sample
size or R-hat wasn't good enough, you usually want to rerun adaptation,
too.)

> * Unlike PyStan, all results are stored in a file structure.

This should be possible in PyStan. We're working on a consistent
set of functionality that we'll implement across (Py/R/Cmd)Stan.
It'll be a while before we get there, though.

> * Each output is uniquely associated to the Stan code, data and seed used. If neither of them change, the result is
> not re-computed.

Nice!

> * This also allows you to execute Stan on another machine, and to copy the output over.
> * StagedStan can parse the summary files of Stan runs, and write data dump files.
> * StagedStan allows the input of data from Python (e.g. numpy arrays).

>
> Perhaps it is useful for someone else too. Fork and play around with it.

Thanks --- and feel free to post back here on updates.

- Bob

messages.author: 51b52a084c2df35c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] StagedStan: Python package for running Stan using compiled executables
parts:
Thank you for your comments, Bob.

When referring to continuation, I did not mean it as fine-grained as you describe.

As you point out, the goals can be achieved with PyStan as well. However, I found the need to control individual stages in more detail (e.g. compile flags, and debugging intermediate products).
Additionally, I had trouble avoiding recompilation and running from initial parameters -- although the API promises that this should be possible. I can't say I have a detailed bug report though.

I was rather confused that the best-fit parameter file that is written by "optimize" can not be used as a init file.
For my problem, the sampling phase hangs for me often for a long time at "Iteration:    1 / 1000 [  0%]  (Warmup)", where I believe it tries to optimize to a good starting point.
So I would like to first optimize, visualize that point, and continue sampling from there, then visualizing the uncertainties.
In StagedStan I implemented reading Stan output files and writing R dump data files, so this is solved this way. Perhaps there is a smarter way I don't know about.

One possible benefit of going through executables (rather than compiling in memory) is that those can be deployed to multiple machines, and the optimized output files can be computed there. That's not so easy to do directly in Python, but with the staged approach, the Python program can pick up the results and continue.
I'm not saying that this can't be achieved by PyStan, but rather that there are two ways of doing it, and they can exist separately.

Speaking of PyStan, accessing the likelihood function would be nice, i.e. evaluating the likelihood + gradient from Python.

Thank you for taking the time.

Cheers,
             Johannes

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] StagedStan: Python package for running Stan using compiled executables
parts:
I ws only commenting in general. I can barely write "hello world"
in Python. We went back and forth between the separate-process
and in-memory version for PyStan and RStan.

I had thought you could access the log prob and gradient from
Python because I know people are using that feature. Maybe it's
not in the latest release? That, by the way, is one of the reasons for
going in-memory!

- Bob
